question.problem:
| $x$ | **$-1$** | **$0$** | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $2$ | $9$ | $0$ | $-9$ | $-12$ |

The vector of coefficients of the curve $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}$ that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the design matrix $X$ in this context?

current_example.problem:
| $x$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $6$ | $3$ | $2$ | $4$ | $6$ |

The vector of coefficients of the curve $y = \beta_0 + \beta_2 x^2 + \beta_3 x^3$ that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14229724/assets/14c0a26b788cdded0306cc5ba7307198b4b90de72e900e27be6622d22543553f.svg)

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector. Find $X$ and $\mathbf{y}$ in this context.
current_example.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$\color{blue}1$** | **$\color{blue}2$** | **$\color{blue}3$** | **$\color{blue}4$** | **$\color{blue}5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $\color{red}6$ | $\color{red}3$ | $\color{red}2$ | $\color{red}4$ | $\color{red}6$ |

The coefficients of the curve

$$
y = \beta_0 + \beta_2 x^2 + \beta_3 x^3
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution ${\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}}$ to the system

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & {1}^{2} & {1}^{3} \\ 1 & {2}^{2} & {2}^{3} \\ 1 & {3}^{2} & {3}^{3} \\ 1 & {4}^{2} & {4}^{3} \\ 1 & {5}^{2} & {5}^{3}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 3 \\ 2 \\ 4 \\ 6\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta$ is the parameter vector, and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector.
